# Security Requirements Quality Checklist: SpamDetector API

**Purpose**: Validate that the SECURITY requirements in the specification are complete, clear,
consistent, and measurable before implementation. This is a "unit test for the requirements" — it
evaluates how the requirements are written, NOT whether the code works.
**Created**: 2026-09-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for every failure mode enumerated in the plan (missing key, empty body, invalid model, auth failure, rate limit, timeout, service error, malformed output, deserialization failure, unexpected error)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK002 Is a requirement specified for the maximum request body size, and is the default value stated numerically? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what MUST NOT appear in logs (API key, credentials, full email body, raw provider payloads)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for what MUST NOT appear in API responses or error messages (key, headers, stack traces, raw exceptions, raw payloads)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the spec define the untrusted-content handling requirement across the entire processing flow, not just at the boundary? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements specified prohibiting external side effects from email content (code execution, HTML render, script exec, link resolution, remote fetch, tool invocation)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK007 Are stateless-processing requirements defined enumerating exactly what MUST NOT be retained (email, history, credentials, conversations, responses)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK008 Is a requirement defined that the provider response MUST be validated against the schema before being returned? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK009 Is the security boundary explicitly defined as "trusted instructions vs. untrusted email content" rather than the delimiter markup? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "fail safely" for invalid/unexpected model output quantified with a concrete outcome (specific status code, no repair)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the meaning of "controlled error" defined precisely enough to distinguish it from an uncontrolled failure (e.g., what a controlled error MUST and MUST NOT contain)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the request-scoped lifetime of the API key stated unambiguously (created per request, not singleton/static/cached)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Constitution §II]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the 30-second provider timeout stated as a specific, testable value rather than "finite"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the terms "sensitive information" and "implementation-sensitive" defined by enumeration so reviewers can objectively judge compliance? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK015 Do the credential-secrecy requirements in the spec (§FR-015, §FR-016) align with the constitution's BYOK Isolation and Security First principles without contradiction? [Consistency, Constitution §I, §II]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the HTTP status-code mapping (400/413/502/500) consistent between the Clarifications, Functional Requirements, and Success Criteria sections? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the requirement that `httpCode` equals the actual HTTP response status stated consistently everywhere it appears? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the "no external effects" requirements consistent between the spec's Minimal External Effects requirement and the edge-case handling of malicious HTML / links? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the prompt-injection handling requirement consistently state that injected content MAY affect the verdict but MUST NOT alter behavior or output format? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality (Measurability)

- [ ] CHK020 Can the requirement "API key never appears in any response, error, or log" be objectively measured, and is a corresponding measurable success criterion defined? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the prompt-injection resistance requirement expressed as a measurable outcome (e.g., 100% of injection cases preserve structure and do not force the verdict)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the "reject before calling the provider" guarantee for missing key / empty body stated as a measurable criterion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK023 Is structured-output conformance expressed as a measurable acceptance criterion (e.g., 100% of successful results conform to the schema)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the timeout behavior expressed measurably (requests exceeding 30s are aborted and return a controlled upstream error)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for the oversized-body scenario (exceeds max size) including the exact rejection status and no provider call? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for an email consisting purely of prompt-injection text? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements defined for hostile input classes named in the plan (malicious HTML, malformed MIME, control characters, very large text)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements defined for the blank/whitespace `x-openai-model` header being treated identically to omitted (default model, no error)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for provider cancellation propagation (client disconnect / request abort)? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK030 Are recovery/no-retry requirements defined so that auth, invalid-model, and malformed-input failures are not retried? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap]

## Dependencies, Assumptions & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK031 Is the assumption that the caller owns and funds the supplied credential documented, along with the requirement that the service never manages/stores it? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the dependency on the external provider's schema-enforcement capability documented, including the fallback requirement when the model does not honor strict output? [Dependency, Gap]
- [ ] CHK033 Is caller-to-service authentication (beyond the BYOK key) explicitly scoped in or out, so its absence is a deliberate decision rather than a gap? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK034 Are logging/observability requirements free of conflict with the PII/secret-exclusion requirements (i.e., no requirement implies logging content that another forbids)? [Conflict, Spec §FR-015, §FR-016]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
